findings.title: Project model fetch failures fully silent in assistant form
findings.problem: getProjectLLMModels now rejects on fetch failure (skipErrorHandling:true + rethrow in src/store/appInfo.ts), but useProjectLLMModels swallows the rejection via `.catch(() => undefined)` with no error state, and LLMSelector (src/pages/assistants/components/AssistantForm/components/LLMSelector.tsx:141) renders the resulting empty model list with no error indicator.
findings.impact: Before this change the same failure still triggered api.ts's generic global toast (skipErrorHandling was not set previously); that toast is now suppressed and nothing replaces it, so a project model fetch failure degrades to a silently empty model dropdown in the assistant form with zero user-visible indication.
findings.recommendation: Surface the failure from useProjectLLMModels (e.g. an error flag/last-error field consumed by LLMSelector) instead of swallowing it unconditionally, or restore a toast specific to this path.

findings.title: Project model fetch failure now blocks whole admin settings form
findings.problem: getProjectLLMModels is awaited inside `Promise.all([getLLMModels(), fetchSettings(), getProjectLLMModels()])`; since it now rejects instead of resolving to [], any project-model fetch failure rejects the whole Promise.all.
findings.impact: The .catch sets loadError(true), which replaces the whole section with 'Unable to load project model settings.' even though the platform catalog and project settings already loaded successfully — an admin can no longer view or edit any model settings for the project on a transient project-model fetch failure, where previously the form still rendered with the rest of the data intact.
findings.recommendation: Catch the getProjectLLMModels() call independently (e.g. `.catch(() => [])` with a partial-data warning) instead of bundling it in the same Promise.all as the settings/catalog fetches that must not be discarded together.
